content.text:
I submitted **index 0 (Bi 0.97, Sb 0.03)** as the best composition. Its EQE was 3.1×10⁻⁴ %, the highest of the three compositions I measured. Every value was very small, though, so none of these films is a good photoanode under 2.4 eV light.

| Index | Bi / Sb | Region | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.97 / 0.03 | Bi-rich end | 3.1×10⁻⁴ |
| 5 | 0.93 / 0.07 | near the Bi₁₂SbO₂₀ phase | 8.7×10⁻⁵ |
| 14 | 0.75 / 0.25 | near the Bi₃SbO₇ phase | −4.7×10⁻⁵ |

- **Trend:** EQE rose steadily toward the Bi-rich end.
- **Structure (XRD):** I measured 2 of the 5 XRD scans. Index 0 has extra peaks (Q ≈ 2.007, 2.32, 3.28 Å⁻¹) that the 50/50 film (index 22) doesn't have. I think these come from a bismuth-oxide-type phase, which may absorb 2.4 eV light better, but I didn't run the phase-matching tool to confirm it.
- **Not measured:** The Sb-rich half of the library, including the BiSbO₄ composition (index 22), never got an EQE measurement. I left it out because EQE was falling as Sb increased. With only 3 measurements, a better composition there can't be ruled out.
